SPRINT 3 — Admin area.

We have merged several teammates' pull requests since the last sprint; get familiar with the current state of the codebase, then add an admin area: an admin role, and an admin-only section to list, search, and manage users (view, promote/demote, deactivate). Ensure only admins can reach it.

Follow proper Ruby on Rails best practices throughout. Write proper automated tests — unit/model tests AND system/feature (Capybara) tests for user-facing flows — and keep them green. Keep the code secure and idiomatic (strong params, scoped queries, authorization, migrations with indexes, no N+1 queries), keep RuboCop/Brakeman/bundle-audit clean, and keep the app runnable. When using a gem whose API you are unsure of (e.g. RubyLLM), study its actual API in the bundle before using it — do not guess method names. Use git: at the END of this task, commit your work with clear, atomic, well-described commit message(s). Do not stop to ask questions; implement fully and finish.


Continue your existing implementation of the task above. Complete missing functionality, fix syntax and boot errors, run the relevant tests, and commit your changes. Use the existing workspace; do not discard its history. Verify the application actually starts and its documented user flow is usable.
Your previous attempt repeatedly rewrote identical files and did not complete the task. Inspect the current files before editing; preserve complete Ruby classes rather than replacing a file with a method fragment. Check syntax, exercise the routes required by the original task, and run the actual test command. Diagnose each concrete failure before another edit. Do not claim a commit or test succeeded unless its command did succeed. Keep server checks bounded so a foreground server does not block your work.
Concrete ordinary failures still need correction: running `ruby -c app/controllers/application_controller.rb` reports an unexpected end near line 32. Inspect the whole class and fix its structure. The test setup does not execute tests; make the selected test framework load the Rails environment and run the actual model and feature tests required above. Use paths under your current project directory, check each changed Ruby file with ruby -c, and verify eager loading with `RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rails runner "Rails.application.eager_load!"`. Finish the original task and verify your git commit succeeds.
